description: .Net GPU compute for the browser and desktop. Write once, run on WebGPU, WebGL, Wasm, CUDA, OpenCL, and CPU.
releaseNotes:
v4.9.5-rc.12: Two GPU-codegen correctness fixes — WebGL GLSL Pow with negative base + integer exponent, and WebGPU WGSL unsigned shift-right of high-bit-set i32-as-uint. Both surfaced 2026-05-04 by lane owners (Data on the WebGL side via DistilBERT/SemanticSearch/GPT-2 cluster; Tuvok on the WebGPU side via OpusRangeDecoderGpu.DecodeBitLogP first-bit divergence). Both were silently producing wrong output across multiple consuming projects.

(1) WebGL: `GLSLCodeGenerator.GenerateCode(BinaryArithmeticValue)` for `BinaryArithmeticKind.PowF` was emitting a bare GLSL `pow(left, right)` call. GLSL ES 3.0 spec defines `pow(x, y)` as undefined for `x < 0`; ANGLE emits the call as `exp(y * log(x))` and `log(negative_x)` is NaN. Every NaN cascades through downstream LayerNorm `(x - mean)^2` -> ReduceMean -> Sqrt -> Mul -> final classifier, suppressing all transformer logits to NaN/zero. Fix: when the exponent is a constant non-negative integer (0..8) detected via `value.Right.Resolve() is PrimitiveValue` and `pf == (int)pf`, expand to repeated multiplication: `pow(x, 2)` becomes `x * x`, `pow(x, 3)` becomes `x * x * x`, etc. Multiplication is well-defined for negative bases. Bound at 8 to avoid bloating GLSL for pathologically large constants. Falls through to native `pow()` past that. Lockdown test `Tests23_PowNegativeBase_IntExp2_NoNaN` exercises pow(x, 2) on values [0.055, -0.037, -1.5, 2.0, -0.001, 3.14, -3.14] — pre-fix WebGL returns NaN for negative inputs; post-fix PASS 7/7. Likely cascade-closes Reference_DistilBERT, Pipeline_SemanticSearch, Reference_GPT2, and possibly Reference_DepthAnything (LayerNorm in transformer/ViT backbones uses (x-mean)^2 universally).

(2) WebGPU: `WGSLKernelFunctionGenerator.GenerateCode(BinaryArithmeticValue)` for `Shl`/`Shr` was emitting `target = left {op} u32(right)` for both kinds. WGSL's `i32 >> u32` is arithmetic (sign-extending) shift; ILGPU stores `uint` as i32 because `BasicValueType` has no UInt32 — so a uint right-shift like `0x80000000u >> 15` came out as `0xFFFF0000` (sign-extended) instead of `0x00010000` (logical). Surfaced by Tuvok's `OpusRangeDecoderGpu_DecodeBitLogP_LogP15Mixed` test on WebGPU — after libopus Init Normalize, `state.Rng = 0x80000000` (high bit set, INT_MIN as i32); the very first `s = r >> logp` step in `DecodeBitLogP` returned the wrong shift, flipping the decoded bit value (`gpu=1, cpu=0`). Fix: when `value.Kind` is Shl or Shr on `Int32` AND (`IsUnsigned` OR `Shl`), emit `target = bitcast<i32>(bitcast<u32>(left) {op} u32(right))`. Symmetric Shl wrap protects against shift-amount UB on validators when the result pushes a 1 into the sign bit; the bit pattern is identical signed-vs-unsigned for Shl, so the bitcast wrap is free correctness. Lockdown tests: `Tests23_UnsignedShr_HighBitNoSignExtend` (pure shift verification of 0x80000000 >> 15 / 1 / 31) and `Tests23_DecodeBitLogP_FirstDecodeShape` (end-to-end mimic of the libopus decoder primitive). Both PASS 7/7 across CPU/CUDA/OpenCL/WebGPU/WebGPUNoSubgroups/Wasm/WebGL post-fix.

UNBLOCKS for Tuvok: every Opus / SILK / CELT / VP9 GPU primitive that does `uint >> int` with a high-bit-set uint operand. Common pattern in range-decoder Normalize, ICDF lookup, bit-decode, transient/silence/intra/post-filter flag decode, and any libopus-shape arithmetic that survives Init's Normalize loop. CELT silence/transient/intra/post-filter flag decodes all use `DecodeBitLogP`, so the WebGPU CELT GPU path is unblocked.

UNBLOCKS for Data: cascade closure of WebGL transformer-cluster failures (DistilBERT + SemanticSearch + GPT-2 + likely DepthAnything mean-drift). Three lockdown tests landed in Tests23 (Pow + Shr + DecodeBitLogP-shape), all 21/21 PASS across all 7 backends. No regressions on existing tests.

v4.9.5-rc.11: Wasm host-write-vs-queued-dispatch race fix. The Wasm dispatcher had a race between host `CopyFromCPU` calls and the copy-IN of a queued (but not yet running) dispatch:

```
buf.CopyFromCPU(data1);   // sync: SharedBuffer = data1
kernel(buf);              // queues D1 (returns immediately, async task in flight)
buf.CopyFromCPU(data2);   // SharedBuffer = data2 NOW
kernel(buf);              // queues D2
await SynchronizeAsync();
```

D1's `RunKernelAsync` ran sync up to the first `await` on `_pendingWork`. If a prior task was in flight, D1's body PAUSED at the await. The caller continued to the second `CopyFromCPU` which OVERWRITES `SharedBuffer`. When D1 resumed, its copy-IN read `SharedBuffer` (= data2 now) instead of data1. D1 ran with the wrong data.

In production this surfaced as **YOLOv8 Wasm Softmax**: Data's per-node capture pinned the first divergence to node 220 (DFL Softmax). Bisect localized to `Scale + Transpose1 + Transpose2` — `SoftmaxOperator.Execute`'s general-axis branch, which calls `TransposeKernel.Transpose` twice. `TransposeKernel` reuses `_paramsBuf` across calls; each call `CopyFromCPU`s its own params. With Scale+T1 already queued, T2's `CopyFromCPU(perm2)` overwrote `paramsBuf.SharedBuffer` BEFORE T1's copy-IN ran. T1 read perm2 instead of perm1 — wrong transpose, wrong final output.

Fix: capture each ArrayView arg's `SharedBuffer` state at QUEUE time (sync, inside `RunKernel` before the task is queued). The dispatch's copy-IN reads from the snapshot SAB instead of `SharedBuffer`. Snapshots are reference-shared across dispatches with the same `HostWriteCounter`, so unchanging buffers (e.g. ML weights uploaded once) only pay the snapshot cost ONCE per host write — not per dispatch. New host-side write allocates a fresh snapshot SAB; old snapshot remains pinned by any in-flight dispatches and is GC'd when none.

API: `WasmMemoryBuffer.GetOrCreateSnapshotForDispatch()` (internal) returns the current snapshot SAB. `WasmAccelerator.RunKernel` walks args at sync time, calls it per ArrayView arg (and per body-struct embedded view via reflection). `RunKernelAsync` accepts a `Dictionary<WasmMemoryBuffer, SharedArrayBuffer> argSnapshots` and uses it in copy-IN.

Lockdown test `Tests23_HostWriteVsQueuedDispatchRace` (Wasm-only failure pre-fix; PASS 7/7 post-fix). Tests23 broader sweep 94/4 — 4 expected failures all in `Tests23_SilkBodyStructShape` (separate distinct codegen bugs tracked individually for follow-up rcs). No regressions on existing tests.

Cascade closes a class of bugs where any consumer reuses a host-written buffer across back-to-back kernel dispatches. SpawnDev.ILGPU.ML's `SoftmaxOperator` general-axis path was the visible victim, but `TransposeKernel`'s reusable `_paramsBuf` pattern is generic — any ML or Codecs kernel doing `CopyFromCPU; queue kernel; CopyFromCPU same buf; queue kernel` was at risk of this race on Wasm. UNBLOCKS: YOLOv8 Wasm Reference test, any future kernel using the dispatch-then-host-rewrite-then-dispatch pattern.

v4.9.5-rc.10: WebGL `glWorker.js` subview-offset uniform leak fix + Wasm OOB diagnostic correctness. Two changes:

(1) `glWorker.js` was conditionally setting the `u_paramX_offset` uniform only when `elementOffset != 0`. WebGL uniforms persist on the program object across draw calls; if dispatch N had `elementOffset=K` (non-zero) for some param, the uniform was set to K. If dispatch N+1 used the SAME program with `elementOffset=0` for that param, the uniform was NOT reset and retained K. The shader read at texelFetch index `K` instead of `0`, producing zeros (or stale values) when the actual data was at index 0 of a different buffer. Fix: always set the offset uniform (default 0). Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Data's StyleMosaic node 55 Gather first-divergent capture: `Mean error 47.29` on WebGL where Gather output was `0` instead of `56`; nodes 0-54 matched WebGPU exactly. Lockdown test `Tests23_SubViewOffsetLeakAcrossDispatches` reads `bufA[2]=300` via `SubView(2,1)` then `bufB[0]=10` via `SubView(0,1)` on the SAME kernel program. Pre-fix on WebGL: second read returns `bufB[2]=30` (offset leaked). Post-fix: returns `bufB[0]=10`. PASS 7/7 across CPU/CUDA/OpenCL/WebGPU/WebGPUNoSubgroups/Wasm/WebGL. Likely cascade-closes the WebGL ML zero-output cluster (5 Style transfers + TextGeneration + DistilBERT + GPT2 + WhisperEncoder + DepthAnything + ConvReluPool + SemanticSearch + BackgroundRemoval + YOLOv8 Reference — any pipeline with sequential same-program dispatches with mixed-offset SubViews).

(2) `WasmAccelerator.cs` OOB diagnostic was computing `dataEnd = vOff + lenCheck * 4` with `4` HARDCODED for byte-per-element. Every view of any element type was reported as 4 bytes per element in the trap log: `ArrayView<long>(1)` showed as 4 bytes (should be 8), `ArrayView<byte>(N)` showed as 4N (4× too big), etc. Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Tuvok's Vp9 trap where V4 (`Allocate1D<long>(1)`) appeared 4 bytes wide, prompting an incorrect rc.9 diagnosis — rc.9's Cast-view fix doesn't apply to a native long buffer because the byte-length compute already used the right element size for that case. The diagnostic was the misleading signal. Fix: track per-view element size in a parallel list, populated from the same `viewElemSizeForLength` that drives the byte-length calculation. Future Wasm OOB investigations on multi-view kernels can trust the trap log directly. Lockdown test `Tests23_NativeLongBuffer` writes `0x1122334455667788L` to a native `Allocate1D<long>(1)` view, reads back. PASS 7/7 across all backends (independent of the diag fix; verifies the underlying allocation is correct and was always correct).

Plus: `Tests23_SilkBodyStructShape` regression test for a 6-short + 9-int body-struct (Tuvok's `SilkDecodeCoreInputs` shape from SpawnDev.Codecs). 5 of 7 backends fail today on this exact shape (WebGPU `Invalid BindGroupLayout`, WebGL `'assign' cannot convert from int to struct_1214`, Wasm `RangeError: Invalid typed array length`, CUDA register-pressure launch-OOR). Test stays in the suite as a multi-backend regression lock; PASS counts will climb as each codegen path gets fixed in subsequent rcs. Each backend's failure mode is distinct and tracked individually.

v4.9.5-rc.9: Wasm cast-view byte-length fix. `WasmAccelerator` was computing a kernel param view's wasm-memory byte range as `iav.Length * wasmBuf.ElementSize` — using the BUFFER's element size rather than the VIEW's. For a `MemoryBuffer1D<int>` (4-byte element) viewed as `ArrayView<long>` via `.Cast<long>()` (8-byte element), this produced byte length `N*4` instead of `N*8` — Wasm reserved only half the bytes the kernel actually accesses, so reads/writes to the back half landed past the allocated range and triggered an OOB. Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Tuvok's `Vp9FrameEntropyKernel` Wasm OOB (`V4=4` bytes wide for `ArrayView<long> outLen`). Fix: extract the view's actual generic-argument element size via reflection (the same logic the SubView byte-offset path already used) and apply it to the byte-length computation. Lockdown test `Tests23_LongViewOverIntBuffer` in `BackendTestBase.Tests23.UintCompareInLoop.cs` writes one long to a Cast<long> view over an int buffer and verifies the round-trip — passes on every backend post-fix. Wasm canary tests (RadixSort + ManyDispatches) green; no regressions.

v4.9.5-rc.8: Wasm body-struct kernel param decomp fix for multi-view containers. `WasmKernelFunctionGenerator.IsViewType` was returning `true` for any struct whose first DirectField is `AddressSpaceType` — including multi-view containers like Tuvok's `VorbisPacketDecodeStaticInputs` (38 ArrayView fields) and any user struct-of-views. Result: the Wasm dispatcher routed multi-view body-struct kernel params through the single-view path, only registering the FIRST view's buffer in `uniqueBuffers`; the remaining N-1 view-pointers in the serialized struct were never written, so the kernel read field 1..N as offset 0 of V0's buffer + the IR field offset (e.g., `s.V1[0]` came back as `V0[4]` consistently across every kernel). Fix: count `AddressSpaceType` fields in `DirectFields`; only return `true` if there's exactly one (real ArrayView/ArrayView1D). Multi-view structs go through the scalar-struct serialization path which already correctly registers each view's buffer via `ExtractBuffersFromStruct`. Verified: Tests21 (BodyStruct_12ArrayViewInt + MixedIntFloat + VariableLength + PerFieldDiagnostic) PASS on Wasm 4/4 (was 4/4 failing pre-fix, e.g., V1[0] returning 100004 instead of 200000). Same fix shape applied to WebGL's `IsMultiDim` heuristic (only set isView=true when NumFields matches a known ArrayView shape: 3, 4, or 6); WebGL Tests21 still need separate per-field-sampler decomposition codegen — gated with sharp technical reason (task #26). Bonus: rc.7's WebGL GLSL fixes carried forward (INT_MIN const + unsigned compare/shift). UNBLOCKS: SpawnDev.Codecs Vorbis Wasm path (38-field VorbisPacketDecodeStaticInputs), upcoming Opus SILK + CELT Wasm decoder primitives, any consumer using struct-of-ArrayView kernel parameters on Wasm.

v4.9.5-rc.7: WebGL GLSL codegen — INT_MIN constant + unsigned-int compare/shift fixes. Three GLSL codegen bugs surfaced by the same Tests23 bisection that closed Tuvok's libopus Normalize loop on rc.6: (1) `GLSLCodeGenerator.GenerateCode(PrimitiveValue)` was substituting `int.MinValue` (bit pattern 0x80000000) with `-2147483647` (bit pattern 0x80000001) as a workaround for an ANGLE/ESSL3 literal-overflow rejection; the substitution silently corrupted every constant that needed the exact 0x80000000 bit pattern (libopus range-coder bounds, IEEE -0.0 bitcasts, all uint shifts that overflow into the high bit). Fix: emit as `int(2147483648u)` — uint-to-int bitcast preserves bits with no parser issue and no UB. (2) `GenerateCode(CompareValue)` for unsigned integer comparisons (`uint <= uintConst`) was emitting bare `int op int` GLSL which triggers signed compare semantics; values with the high bit set compared as negative. Fix: cast operands to uint when `IsUnsignedOrUnordered` flag is set. (3) `GenerateCode(BinaryArithmetic)` for Shl/Shr where the result would overflow into the sign bit hit GLSL ES 3.0 signed-shift undefined behavior; ANGLE produces inconsistent results. Fix: emit as `int(uint(left) op uint(right))` for Shl unconditionally and Shr when IsUnsigned (preserves sign-extension for signed Shr). Plus `glWorker.js` TF readback now uses `Uint8Array` for raw byte readback (was `Float32Array`; cosmetic — the byte path is identical, but explicit Uint8Array is clearer and avoids any future driver-side type-conversion paths). Verified: Tests22 14/14 PASS + Tests23 49/49 PASS across all backends. WebGL test sweep 457/1/123 — the 1 fail is the preexisting `LocalMemoryRepro_Int64_ShortByteViews` architectural-varying-count ceiling, NOT caused by this fix. Likely fixes a chunk of Data's 12 ML WebGL correctness failures (uint compares were a major contributor).

v4.9.5-rc.6: ILGPU LoopUnrolling shift-induction trip-count fix. Surfaced 2026-05-04 by Tuvok's libopus-style Normalize while-loop pattern (`while (rng <= 0x800000) rng <<= 8`) which silently produced wrong output (Rng=0 instead of 0x80000000) on every GPU and Wasm + WebGL backend; CPU bypassed because it doesn't run the unroller. Root cause: `LoopInfo.TryGetTripCount` adjusted the per-iteration multiplier for shift updates by `update *= 2`, which only produces the correct value for `<<= 1`. For `<<= N` with N != 1 the multiplier should be `2^N`, NOT `2*N`. With shift_count=8 the trip count came out as 5 instead of 3, and the unroller emitted two extra `rng <<= 8` operations past the loop's intended exit, leaving rng=0 in the final state. Fix: change to `update = 1 << update` with bounds check (1 <= shift < 32). Bounded trip-count is identical for shift_count==1 (preserves behavior of every previous correct case). Verification: full Tests22 set (libopus Init/Normalize regression) PASSES on every backend post-fix (was 12/14 failing). Algorithm sweep across Reduce / Initialize / RadixSort / Sequence / Scan / Histogram / Algorithm* — 481/0/93 in 53m48s, zero regressions. Includes also rc.5's WebGPU storage-buffer binding-count coalesce (Tuvok's 38-ArrayView VorbisPacketDecodeStaticInputs → 2 coalesced bindings) — see rc.5 notes for that surface. New bisection regression tests `BackendTestBase.Tests23.UintCompareInLoop.cs` 6 cases lock down the unroll-path codegen against future regressions; the WebGL-only Tests23 failures are gated via UnsupportedTestException for a separate pre-existing GLSL signed-shift/compare codegen issue (NOT this fix). See _DevComms/SpawnDev.ILGPU/geordi-to-tuvok-tests22-fix-found-2026-05-04.md.
